response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT o.mktnote AS pair, AVG(f.feerate - f.rebrate) AS avg_net FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = f.orderslink GROUP BY o.mktnote), b AS (SELECT AVG(avg_net) AS bench FROM g) SELECT AVG(g.avg_net) AS avg_of_above_benchmark_pairs, AVG(g.avg_net - b.bench) AS avg_excess_over_benchmark FROM g CROSS JOIN b WHERE g.avg_net > b.bench

assumptions.assumption: A fee's net rate is NULL if either feerate or rebrate is NULL, so that fee is skipped in the per-pair average. A pair whose fees are all NULL has a NULL average and is skipped in the benchmark.
Each fee is joined to its order by plain equality on recordvault = orderslink. If recordvault has duplicate values, a fee would be counted once per matching order row.
All NULL mktnote values form one group, as GROUP BY does by default. Empty-string or differently-cased pair names stay separate groups.
